status: VERIFIED - re-verified 2026-08-15 after the OPEN-11 attrition mitigation: full-file load (31,324 rows, no completion filter; 25,025 rows carry at least one observed outcome); 18 arms (17 interventions + Control); 17x12 = 204 ATE cells, 0 NaN; sealed/attrition_bounds.csv carved alongside. Codings unchanged from the previous VERIFIED state (donation/newsletter/petition/letter checked against Advocacy_Cleaning_main.ipynb; all moderator level strings equal to ssb.spec.load()['moderators']).
sample_description: 25,025 U.S. adults (Connect/Prime panel, 2023-24) who reached the outcome block, out of 31,324 post-exclusion randomised respondents (22,374 of them finished the whole survey). Each was randomly assigned to one of 17 climate-advocacy interventions or a neutral control video. Interventions are long and heterogeneous in modality: reading tasks, Twitter-feed and magazine-article stimuli, writing tasks, and videos (3-12 minutes; median condition duration 150-390 s). Outcomes are measured immediately after, in a randomised DV order, and mix 0-100 sliders, real 0/1 behaviours (petition signature, newsletter sign-up, letter written), and a real $0-10 donation.

belief_1.question: belief in climate change (0-100 slider; BeliefandPolicySupport block; item wording NOT in the codebook)

policy_1.question: climate policy support (0-100 slider; BeliefandPolicySupport block; item wording NOT in the codebook)

pol_campaign.question: stated commitment to support a climate-focused political campaign (0-100 slider)

pol_candidate.question: stated commitment to vote for a climate-focused candidate (0-100 slider; asked only of respondents eligible to vote)

march.question: stated commitment to attend a climate march (0-100 slider)

conversation.question: stated commitment to have a conversation about climate change (0-100 slider)

petition.question: BEHAVIOUR: signed a real climate petition (0/1)

newsletter1.question: BEHAVIOUR: signed up for climate organisation newsletter #1 (0/1) - closest analogue of the target's newsletter_signup

newsletter2.question: BEHAVIOUR: signed up for climate organisation newsletter #2 (0/1)

newsletter.question: BEHAVIOUR: signed up for at least one of the two newsletters (0/1, = newsletter1 OR newsletter2) [de-zero-filled: 0 for people who never reached the block, so masked to NaN unless a real-NaN DV column is present]

letter.question: BEHAVIOUR: wrote a letter to an elected representative (0/1, completion coded by GPT and manually checked) [de-zero-filled: 0 for people who never reached the block, so masked to NaN unless a real-NaN DV column is present]

donation.question: BEHAVIOUR: dollars of a $10 bonus donated to an environmental organisation ($0-10; 99.7% whole dollars) - same units as the target's donation_ams

gender.note: survey item; only Male/Female occur in the released file (codebook codes 3 prefer-not and 4 non-binary/other are absent), so the target's `Other` level is not represented

party.note: the survey item has only Democrat/Republican/Other - there is NO Independent option, and 29% of respondents chose `Other`, which must therefore be a mixture of true independents and true others. `Other` is deliberately LEFT UNMAPPED (-> NaN) rather than passed through as the target's `Other`, which is a ~3% residual category

education.note: panel-provider column, populated for only 41.5% of finishers (the Connect sub-panel); maps exactly onto all six target levels. `Prefer not to say` left unmapped

income.note: panel-provider column, 41.5% of finishers. Two of the 18 provider bands STRADDLE a target cut point and are deliberately left unmapped rather than guessed: `$50,000-$59,999` crosses $56,000 and `$150,000-$174,999` crosses $168,000. That drops ~13% of the covered subsample, so the income distribution here is dented at those two points

moderators_unavailable.race: the only race column is the panel provider's `Race` (41.5% of finishers). It has no Hispanic/Latino level - Hispanic identity lives in a SEPARATE `Hispanic` column - so the target's 5-level race variable cannot be built from any single column, and building it from `Race` alone would silently classify Hispanic respondents as White/Other. Left out; a two-column recode is not expressible in this adapter format.
moderators_unavailable.party_independent: see moderators.party note - the target's Independent level does not exist in this study.
moderators_unavailable.income_two_bands: see moderators.income note - $50,000-$59,999 and $150,000-$174,999 are unmapped.

provenance.readme_claims: readme.txt + Advocacy_Cleaning_main.ipynb: exclusions (test ResponseIds, blank/duplicate aid, AttentionCheck_purp != 4) already applied to advocacy_data.csv; ~1,733-1,745 per arm; belief_1/policy_1 16.5%-35% missing by arm.
caveats: DIFFERENTIAL ATTRITION IS THE HEADLINE PROBLEM, and it is now bounded rather than filtered away. Only 22,374 of 31,324 (71.4%) finished and 25,025 (79.9%) reached the outcome block; both vary by arm (completion 61.2%-79.5%, observation 67.5%-86.7%), and the long writing/video arms lose the most people. Any conditioning on having answered is POST-TREATMENT. Lee (2009) trimming bounds are carved alongside the truth; they are ~10.6 pp wide against a median |ATE| of 2.5 pp and identify the sign of only 32.8% of cells. Rank order is the transferable signal; magnitudes are not.

`newsletter`, `letter` and `donation_bin` are coded 0 (not NaN) for people who never reached the question, while `petition`, `newsletter1`, `newsletter2`, `donation` carry real NaN. This adapter fixes that with `observed_if_any` (mask to NaN unless a real-NaN DV column is present) instead of the old `Finished == 1` filter; an unfixed unfiltered ATE on `newsletter`/`letter` would be a pure attrition artefact.
belief_1 and policy_1 are NOT in the codebook; only their block name (`BeliefandPolicySupport`) is known. Exact item wording is UNVERIFIED.
Dose is wildly unequal: readable stimulus length ranges from 283 chars (control) to 11,825 chars (IndStructuralChange). Content and dose are confounded.
Modality differs from the target: videos and writing tasks vs the target's short read-a-message design. Use for ordering, not magnitudes (the source README says the same).
No trust-in-scientists item of any kind.
`Country Of Residence` is populated for only 10,568 of 31,324 rows (it is a panel-provider column), so it CANNOT be used as a filter; the study is US-only by design.
The authors' own estimates are mixed-effects with FDR correction; this adapter computes raw differences in means.

Outcomes DROPPED on purpose: `video` (asked only of social-media users, 72.8% of finishers), `flyless` (59.5%), `lessbeef` (89.2%), `bank` (conditional on bankscore, 81.8%), `donation_bin` (redundant with donation and NaN-coded-as-0), and the four 0-1 composites (`public_awareness`, `political_advocacy`, `financial_advocacy`, `lifestyle_changes`), which average items with different missingness.

Moderator carves are still effectively finisher-only: Gender/Age/Party are asked at the END of the survey and are present for only ~20% of the 2,651 reached-but-unfinished respondents, so they drop out of any moderator grouping. The marginal ATE therefore uses a slightly larger sample than the moderator ATEs - deliberate, and recorded here.
provenance.target_relevance: the ONLY training dataset carrying both of the target's non-slider outcomes in the target's own units: `donation` is $0-10 and `newsletter1`/`newsletter2` are 0/1 sign-ups. See inputs/measured/goldwert2026_format.json.
provenance.harness_note: ssb.task.true_ates(df, ad, moderator='education') raises ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer, because the `Less than high school` level has 0-5 respondents in some arms and wm() returns NaN for n<=2, which the int(an) cast cannot take. This is a harness limitation, not an adapter error (marginal ATEs and the gender/age_band/party/income moderator carves all work). Left unmodified per instruction. Workaround if an education carve is needed: cast with a nullable Int64 in true_ates, or temporarily drop the two thinnest education levels from the map.

attrition_note: OPEN item 11 mitigation, chosen and measured 2026-08-15. The `Finished == 1` filter is REMOVED and replaced by per-outcome de-zero-filling (`observed_if_any`), because the filter was solving the zero-fill inconsistency by throwing away data AND tightening the post-treatment conditioning. Measured on the full randomised file: the analysis sample rises 22,374 -> 25,025; the mean Lee-bound trim fraction falls 0.110 -> 0.094; the mean bound width falls 12.54 -> 10.57 pp and the share of cells whose SIGN the bounds identify rises 0.270 -> 0.328. ATEs move by 0.55 pp on average (max 4.70) and correlate 0.977 with the filtered ones, so the ORDERING is unchanged. Per-arm observation rates run 0.675 (LetterFuture) to 0.867 (HopeAngerNarratives) against control 0.750; completion rates run 0.612 to 0.795 against control 0.642. `carve` writes sealed/attrition_bounds.csv. The bounds are ~10.6 pp wide against a median |ATE| of ~2.5 pp: this task's MAGNITUDES ARE NOT IDENTIFIED by the data, so it must not be pooled into the calibration slope on equal terms - it is a separate calibration family.
